newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares boosted by OMV and Boehler.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares boosted by OMV and Boehler.

text.p: Austrian shares kicked off the week on a buoyant note, ending 0.6 percent higher on Monday due to demand for oil and chemicals group OMV and high-grade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm.
Traders said underlying market sentiment remains positive, but that resistance on the ATX index of 21 blue chips is seen at around 1,183 to 1,185 points.
"There's resistance at 1,083/85 -- it's questionable whether we can breach that with the current preference for stockpicking," said one trader.
The ATX gained 7.54 points to close 1,182.16 with 12 shares advancing, eight falling, and one unchanged.
Of continuously-traded shares, 12 gained, 11 fell and one was unchanged.
Traders said the extended trading session -- lengthened by one hour from today -- had little impact on the day's turover.
"But in future it should help (increase turnover) as we'll then have a chance to react to economic data out of the U.S.," said one trader.
The day's best performer was oil and chemicals group OMV, rising 2.23 percent to 1,340 ahead of the release of their full-year earnings, expected on Wednesday.
The leading decliner was Wolford, down 3.04 percent at 1,435.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index added on 0.65 percent to 442.02.
The February ATX future rose 8.2 points to 1,184 on 767 contracts traded.
